chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said:

Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) was asked - it was said to him: How was your morning, O son of the Messenger of God? He said: I awoke with a Lord above me, the Fire before me, death seeking me, and the Reckoning staring at me. I am held hostage by my deeds. I cannot find what I love, nor can I repel what I hate. The affairs are in the hand of one other than me - if He wills, He may punish me, and if He wills, He may pardon me. Which poor person is poorer than me?!

key_terms.فقير: Poor, needy before God - spiritual poverty expressing absolute dependence on God
key_terms.محدق: Staring intently, encompassing, closing in on all sides
key_terms.مرتهن: Held hostage, pledged - one whose fate is determined by their deeds, as collateral is held for a debt

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Husayn say about his spiritual state before God?
ai.summary: Imam al-Husayn ibn Ali (AS) describes his morning state in response to being asked 'How are you?' by expressing his profound awareness of God's sovereignty over him: the Fire before him, death pursuing him, the Reckoning encircling him, and his complete dependence on his Lord. This statement exemplifies the Imam's servitude ('ubudiyyah) before God, reflecting the intense spiritual humility that characterized the Ahl al-Bayt despite their exalted spiritual rank. The historical audience would have understood this as a teaching on true God-consciousness (taqwa) and spiritual poverty (faqr) before God.
